overall: The AG found violations for failing to announce reconvening in open session after executive session (Sept. 29, 2010) and for an insufficiently specific notice (Oct. 12, 2010); no violation on off-notice discussion or the Police Chief's participation. The rescission request was declined because the no-trespass order had been lifted.

allegations.summary: Board discussed and voted on a police-raised topic at its Sept. 29, 2010 meeting that was not on the posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: While the Board acted within the law in deliberating on a topic which was not listed on the meeting notice

allegations.summary: Board did not announce at the Sept. 29, 2010 meeting whether open session would reconvene after executive session, and the door stayed closed.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the public body failed to announce to the public whether it would reconvene in open session.

allegations.summary: Oct. 12, 2010 notice listed only 'Police Chief Update' and 'Discuss Alleged Open Meeting Law Violation' without identifying the specific complaint discussed.
allegations.key_passage: If a public body anticipates discussing an Open Meeting Law complaint in open session, then they should list that topic in the meeting notice with sufficient detail to inform the public of the details of the complaint.

allegations.summary: Police Chief was allowed to address an Open Meeting Law complaint at the Oct. 12, 2010 meeting, which complainant said should not have occurred.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, whether to permit the Police Chief to address the complaint was entirely at the discretion of the Board.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law; similar conduct in the future may be considered an intentional violation.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and may consider similar conduct in the future to be an intentional violation of the law.
